Jordan — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a compact evidence pack and a telemetry matrix to address these points (see attachments: airlock-telemetry-evidence.zip, telemetry_matrix.csv). Below is an executive summary; the attached CSV has the row-level detail you asked for.

Executive summary:
- Categories: Our private runtime emits three logical categories: operational telemetry (agent/operator heartbeats, health checks, agent logs), usage metadata (per-request non-payload metadata: timestamp, model id, token counts, latency, route id), and diagnostic traces (stack traces/crash artifacts). We do not log prompt or response payloads by default in Private deployments.
- Storage: By default telemetry is written to the local operator-controlled filesystem under /var/lib/redwood/telemetry and can be configured to an on-prem object store (S3-compatible) for retention. All telemetry at rest is encrypted with the node-local key, and we offer integration with customer KMS for envelope encryption.
- Retention: The product ships with a default 90-day retention for usage and operational metrics; diagnostic traces are kept 30 days by default. Retention is configurable via the operator config (retention.days) up to 3650 days (10 years) subject to local storage capacity and customer policy.
- Phone-home: For Private (VPC/on-prem/air-gapped) installations the default configuration does NOT phone-home. No telemetry is sent to Redwood control plane unless the customer enables one of the optional support features: (1) periodic anonymized health-heartbeat (1x/24h) for proactive support, or (2) managed telemetry upload for case-specific troubleshooting. Both features are OFF by default and require customer opt-in plus an outbound proxy configuration.
- Audit/export bundle: We provide a signed tarball (GZIP) that contains: telemetry CSVs, operator logs, a manifest.json (sha256 checksums) and an anonymization log. Bundles are produced by the operator CLI as a single file (example name: telemetry_export_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.tar.gz). The bundle is signed with the customer's GPG key (if configured) or with a local HSM-backed signing key; we provide a mode that redacts request/response payloads and obfuscates user identifiers. Typical size estimate: 150–400 MB per 30 days for medium throughput sites (10k requests/day).

Irene is looping in the operator-runbook and Vanessa will chime in on KMS/retention policy options if you want to discuss billing/contract implications for extended retention.

If you need, we can produce a 30-minute technical walkthrough this week and a sample export bundle from a sanitized dev instance for your auditors.

Jordan — confirmed. Answers inline below and I attached a sanitized sample bundle for your auditors (Helios_telemetry_sample_bundle.tar.gz).

1) Stored-field names / CSV columns:
- operator_logs.log (plain text roll files; fields: timestamp, level, component, message_id, message)
- telemetry_requests.csv (columns: ts_iso, route_id, model_id, request_id, token_count, latency_ms, outcome_code)
- diagnostic_traces/ (directory of .trace files named by trace_id and ts)
- manifest_sha256.txt (sha256 for every file in the bundle)

We included a sample telemetry_requests.csv in the bundle and a sample parsing rule in the CSV header. If you need different column names for SIEM compatibility we can add a mapping layer in the operator ingest pipeline (configurable).

2) Signatures: Redwood supports detached signatures (RFC 4880/PGP detached sig) and a sha256 manifest. The operator export command supports --sign-detached and --sign-key <key-id>. Customers can supply a keypair to the operator (we accept GPG public keys via the operator config). If no customer key is provided the bundle will be signed with a node-local HSM-protected key; both produce a detached .sig file and a manifest SHA256.

3) Audit records: The operator audit log (audit.log) records export creation time, operator username, CLI arguments, and an upload record (uploader identity and destination) when upload is enabled. The export_event entry includes the exported file name and the sha256 checksum. We also log IP of the initiator when the network is enabled.

We attached: Helios_telemetry_sample_bundle.tar.gz (7.4 MB; sanitized), inside you will find telemetry_requests.csv, operator_logs.log, manifest_sha256.txt, and telemetry_export_20280527.sig (detached signature).
